definition: Source credibility is the perceived trustworthiness or reliability of the person or source providing information, and it is a key part of how people judge whether information is believable. In this research context, it refers to the positive or negative credibility evaluations people make about a source.

reasons: The packet supports source credibility as positive or negative evaluations of a source, but it does not explicitly support the broader definition as the perceived trustworthiness or reliability of the person or source providing information.
The claim that source credibility is a key part of how people judge whether information is believable is not stated in the packet in that form and is too generalized beyond the supplied text.
The packet does not define source credibility as “perceived trustworthiness or reliability” or explicitly link it to “how people judge whether information is believable.”

The packet supports that the study involves making “positive or negative source credibility evaluations,” but it does not provide support for the broader wording about perceived trustworthiness/reliability or believability judgments.
